newsitem.title: USA: Senate confirms U.S. ambassador to Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Senate confirms U.S. ambassador to Vietnam.

text.p: The Senate voted on Thursday to confirm Douglas "Pete" Peterson as the first post-war U.S. ambassador to Vietnam.

President Bill Clinton nominated Peterson for the post last May. Peterson, a former Democratic congressman from Florida, served as a fighter pilot in Vietnam and was held prisoner by Hanoi for more than six years. The long-delayed approval came after a brief debate and without a recorded vote.

Peterson's nomination had been held up by Sen Bob Smith, a New Hampshire Republican, who charged Vietnam was not cooperating fully with efforts to account for Americans servicemen still missing after the war in Southeast Asia.
Peterson's confirmation was strongly supported by Republican Sen John McCain of Arizona, a former Navy pilot whon was also held prisoner in Vietnam.
Smith said he had received a letter from President Clinton's National Security Adviser Sandy Berger promising that Washington would continue pressing the Vietnamese for information.

"Through this event we can confirm that now the majority of American people and (the) government in general agree to build up a new kind of relationship with Vietnam." he said. "Of course we are pleased."
The U.S. Senate on Thursday confirmed Peterson's appointment after a brief debate and without a recorded vote.

His nomination, nearly 22 years after the Vietnam war ended, had been held up first by a legal technicality and then by charges that Hanoi's efforts to account for Americans missing in action in Vietnam were inadequate.

Phong dismissed the delays in the process and said Hanoi understood the domestic political environment in Washington which had caused it. "Because of the delay the achievement is more significant," he said.
